title: Excluded-grid treewidth exponent
formal: Determine the excluded-grid exponent \(x_{\mathrm{grid}}\) to absolute error at most \(1/100\). For each integer \(r\ge2\), let \[f(r)=\min\{t\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}:\forall G,\ \operatorname{tw}(G)\ge t\Longrightarrow Q_r\text{ is a minor of }G\},\] where \(G\) ranges over finite simple undirected graphs and \(Q_r\) is the \(r\)-by-\(r\) square grid. Define \[x_{\mathrm{grid}}=\inf\{a\ge0:f(r)=O(r^a)\}.\] The precise asymptotic quantifiers, treewidth and ordinary graph-minor model are given below. The parameter \(r\) is grid side length, not its \(r^2\) vertices. Logarithmic factors are outside the requested precision.
definitions:
Graphs and grids. A finite simple undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) has a finite vertex set and an edge set consisting of unordered pairs of distinct vertices; there are no loops or parallel edges. The vertex set of \(Q_r\) is \(\{1,\ldots,r\}^2\), and two vertices \((i,j)\) and \((i',j')\) are adjacent exactly when
\[|i-i'|+|j-j'|=1.\]
Thus \(r\) counts the side length, while the grid has \(r^2\) vertices. Host graphs may be disconnected and have arbitrary order, degree and genus.

Minor containment. A graph \(H\) is a minor of \(G\) if there are nonempty vertex subsets \((B_v)_{v\in V(H)}\) of \(V(G)\) such that they are pairwise disjoint, each induced graph \(G[B_v]\) is connected, and for every edge \(uv\in E(H)\) an edge of \(G\) joins \(B_u\) to \(B_v\). These subsets are called branch sets. Extra edges inside or between branch sets are allowed. Equivalently, one may delete vertices and edges and contract edges, then remove loops and merge parallel edges. This is ordinary minor containment, with no prescribed roots, induced-subgraph condition or topological-minor requirement.

Treewidth. A tree decomposition of \(G\) consists of a finite nonempty tree \(T\) and bags \(X_t\subseteq V(G)\) for its nodes such that every vertex lies in a bag, both endpoints of every edge lie together in a bag, and for each vertex the nodes whose bags contain it form a nonempty connected subtree of \(T\). A tree is a connected acyclic undirected graph. The decomposition width is \(\max_{t\in V(T)}|X_t|-1\). The treewidth \(\operatorname{tw}(G)\) is the minimum width over all such decompositions. In particular, the empty graph has treewidth \(-1\) under this convention and has no effect on thresholds \(t\ge0\).

Extremal threshold. The qualitative Grid-Minor Theorem ensures that the defining set of thresholds is nonempty. Since treewidth is integer valued,
\[f(r)=1+\max\{\operatorname{tw}(G):G\text{ is a finite simple undirected graph with no }Q_r\text{ minor}\}.\]
This maximum exists: its set of integer values is nonempty and bounded above by the qualitative theorem. It is a maximum of widths, not a bound on the number of vertices of a grid-excluding graph. Arbitrarily large trees, for example, do not contain \(Q_r\) for \(r\ge2\).

Exponent convention. Define \[x_{\mathrm{grid}}=\inf\{a\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}:\exists C>0\ \exists r_0\ge2\ \forall r\in\mathbb Z_{\ge r_0},\ f(r)\le Cr^a\}.\] The known polynomial Grid-Minor Theorem makes this set nonempty; the cited ninth-power bound with polylogarithmic overhead gives \(x_{\mathrm{grid}}\le9\), and the quadratic-logarithmic lower bound gives \(x_{\mathrm{grid}}\ge2\). The exponent is equivalently the limit superior of \(\log f(r)/\log r\); no ordinary limit or attainment of the infimum is assumed. In particular, exponent two permits a growing logarithmic factor and does not assert \(f(r)=O(r^2)\). Constants may depend on a chosen positive slack in the exponent, but not on the grid side length or host graph. This is a structural existence exponent, not a running-time exponent for finding a grid.
answer_criterion: Supply an unambiguously specified real answer \(a_*\) and a complete Lean-checked proof of absolute error at most \(1/100\) in the defined exponent. A certified enclosing interval of width at most \(1/50\) qualifies via its midpoint. Both sides of the interval must be justified. An exact value also qualifies. The infimum need not be attained, and no ordinary logarithmic growth limit is assumed. Matching logarithmic factors, leading constants and an algorithm attaining the endpoint exponent are not required. A one-sided improvement alone qualifies only if the resulting certified interval is sufficiently narrow.
why: The Grid-Minor Theorem connects an abstract measure of graph connectivity with a concrete planar pattern. Its quantitative loss controls the strength of many structural and parameterized-algorithm results. Determining the optimal loss would identify how much treewidth is inherently needed to force a grid in unrestricted graphs, including whether the remaining logarithmic obstruction captures the whole difficulty.

progress.text: Robertson and Seymour prove that excluding any fixed planar minor bounds treewidth.
The lower-bound construction yields \(f(r)=\Omega(r^2\log r)\), as reported in the later primary papers.
Chekuri and Chuzhoy establish the first polynomial relationship and a randomized grid-finding algorithm.
Chuzhoy and Tan improve the general upper bound to \(O(r^9\operatorname{polylog}r)\).
The product-structure strengthening separates the treewidth of an underlying graph from an excluded-graph-dependent clique blow-up.
The SODA 2026 result makes the fixed-minor grid bound polynomial in the size of the additional excluded graph and linear in grid side length.
The disjoint-paths preprint improves linkage and rooted-minor irrelevant-vertex bounds, with different quantified parameters.
ICALP 2026 publishes polynomial bounds for the structure of graphs excluding an annotated grid.

status_note: Checked on 16 September 2026. The inspected primary literature supports the general bounds \(\Omega(r^2\log r)\) and \(O(r^9\operatorname{polylog}r)\). The June 2026 revision of the product-structure paper still cites the latter general bound. The SODA 2026 fixed-minor result, ICALP 2026 annotated result and May 2026 linkage preprint have different additional promises or targets; none inspected supplies matching bounds for f(r). No general resolution was found in the bounded later-work search. This review checked theorem statements and their scope, without independently verifying the long proofs.

context_blocks.text: Treewidth records the smallest possible largest bag in a tree decomposition, minus one. Many graph algorithms can process small bags efficiently even when the whole graph is large. A grid is a canonical obstruction to small treewidth. The qualitative theorem says that sufficiently large treewidth forces any fixed grid as a minor; the unresolved issue is the optimal dependence on grid size.

The grid \(Q_r\) itself has treewidth \(r\), but this does not imply a linear threshold for arbitrary host graphs. The complete graph on \(r^2-1\) vertices has treewidth \(r^2-2\), yet cannot contain a minor with \(r^2\) vertices. Thus \(f(r)\ge r^2-1\). Branch sets can contract large parts of a host, but they must remain pairwise disjoint and nonempty.

The established lower bound is stronger: \(f(r)=\Omega(r^2\log r)\). The cited work attributes it to Robertson, Seymour and Thomas using constant-degree expanders of logarithmic girth. Such graphs combine treewidth proportional to their order with long shortest cycles; a large grid minor forces many disjoint cycles in the host. The extra logarithmic obstruction survives even for sparse graphs.

Chekuri and Chuzhoy first made the relationship polynomial. Their theorem is stated in the reverse direction: treewidth \(k\) guarantees grid side length at least a constant times \(k^{1/98}\) divided by a fixed power of \(\log k\). Equivalently, it gives an upper bound \(f(r)=O(r^{98}\operatorname{polylog}r)\). Confusing side length with vertex count, or the threshold with this inverse guarantee, changes the exponents.

The selected numerical exponent distinguishes polynomial scales while ignoring logarithmic factors. In particular, a proved \(r^2\operatorname{polylog}r\) upper bound together with the known lower bound would give exponent exactly two and answer this card.

Chuzhoy and Tan prove \(f(r)\le Cr^9(\log r)^c\) for absolute constants \(C,c>0\). Together with the quadratic-logarithmic lower bound, this places the requested exponent in \([2,9]\). These are bounds recorded in the cited literature; the present formulation review does not certify a fresh catalogue-wide status audit.

Robertson, Seymour and Thomas predicted growth \(\Theta(r^2\log r)\), whereas Demaine and coauthors predicted cubic growth. These predictions would yield numerical exponents two and three respectively. Determining the exponent to absolute error \(1/100\) is the selected target; settling lower-order factors is not required.

The Grid-Minor Theorem Revisited gives a finer structural description: graphs excluding a fixed planar graph embed as subgraphs of clique blow-ups of graphs of controlled treewidth. A clique blow-up replaces each vertex by a fixed-size complete graph and every original edge by all edges between the corresponding cliques. The factor controlling the clique size may depend on the excluded graph, so the theorem does not determine this card’s optimal numerical dependence on grid side length.

Catching Rats in H-minor-free Graphs proves that excluding both a fixed graph \(H\) and \(Q_r\) gives treewidth \(O(g_H r+t^{2304})\), where \(t=|V(H)|\) and \(g_H\) is the Euler genus of \(H\). Euler genus is the minimum value \(2-\chi\) of a closed connected surface admitting an embedding, with \(\chi\) its Euler characteristic. Since \(g_H=O(t^2)\), the paper also gives \(O(t^2r+t^{2304})\). For fixed \(H\), the dependence on \(r\) is linear.

The additional exclusion in that theorem matters. General host graphs do not avoid a common fixed \(H\). Choosing \(H=Q_r\) is allowed for a grid-excluding graph, but then \(H\) varies with \(r\) and \(t=r^2\); it cannot yield a linear universal threshold. This distinction prevents a sharp special-class result from being mistaken for a solution of the all-graphs problem.

The ICALP 2026 paper studies a designated set of vertices and grid models whose every branch set meets that set. It obtains polynomial bounds for the corresponding structural decomposition. Those bounds concern an annotated generalization and are not a matching estimate of the ordinary threshold defined here. Additional structure in a decomposition and an optimal numerical treewidth bound are different conclusions.

The May 2026 disjoint-paths preprint sharpens bounds for vital linkages and for vertices whose deletion preserves bounded-size rooted-minor information. Its parameters include the number of terminals and the size of a grid rooted on an annotated set. Despite the phrase “Optimal Bounds” in the title, its theorems do not claim a constant-factor characterization of the unrestricted excluded-grid threshold.

Sharper general grid bounds affect the quantitative consequences of routing, packing-versus-covering results and parameterized algorithms. Their role is to turn sufficiently large treewidth into a usable grid, or to bound treewidth when such a grid is absent. Matching lower bounds would also identify an unavoidable limitation of that structural implication.

sentences: The Grid-Minor Theorem forces a large square grid minor when treewidth is sufficiently large.
The extremal threshold is measured against the side length of that grid.
The card asks for the polynomial growth exponent of this threshold to absolute accuracy 0.01.
A grid of side length r has r squared vertices, so the parameter convention matters.
Logarithmic factors and the exact threshold function are not part of this numerical target.

source_formulation.text: Preserves importance 96 and determination of the all-graphs excluded-grid threshold up to universal constant factors, including logarithmic dependence. The parameter is grid side length, not its vertex count. The threshold convention tw(G)≥f(r) is equivalent to one plus the maximum treewidth among excluding graphs. The 2016 paper uses the inverse parameterization, guaranteed side length from treewidth; its bounds are translated accordingly. No polynomial-time construction requirement is added.
